selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline mount/config state before any changes
selected_evidence.summary: Showed /tmp had no separate mount and /dev/shm lacked noexec before hardening

selected_evidence.requirement: fstab updated with hardened options for /tmp and /dev/shm
selected_evidence.summary: Backed up fstab then appended bind/tmpfs entries with noexec,nosuid,nodev

selected_evidence.requirement: Discovery that bind mount needs an explicit remount step, and creation of persistent systemd remount unit
selected_evidence.summary: Proved mount -a alone doesn't apply bind options; added and enabled tmp-hardening.service which correctly remounts /tmp with the required flags

selected_evidence.requirement: Live functional proof that exec, setuid, and device nodes are ignored on /tmp and /dev/shm (pre-restart)
selected_evidence.summary: Script execution returned exit 126 on both mounts; device node read returned Permission denied on both mounts (nosuid covered by findmnt option confirmation since noexec already blocks all execution including setuid binaries)

selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity + mount state) for node1
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 1f0657c2-c163-4ef6-be0b-3118b10aa595 plus findmnt output confirming hardened options and enabled/active service, prior to restart
Backgrounded sudo reboot command with a 2s delay; exec call returned REBOOT_TRIGGERED successfully before the node disconnected

selected_evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
selected_evidence.summary: boot_id was unchanged, then connection was refused during reboot, then boot_id returned as 4b123f3b-ec2e-4211-8c68-982213933b4d, a different value confirming an actual restart

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: hardened mount options persisted and service is healthy
selected_evidence.summary: findmnt confirms both /tmp and /dev/shm retain nosuid,nodev,noexec after reboot; tmp-hardening.service is enabled and active (exited 0) post-boot

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart functional proof that exec/device restrictions are enforced
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot, script execution on /tmp and /dev/shm again returned exit 126, and device-node reads again returned Permission denied on both mounts

commands.command:
cat <<'EOF' | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/tmp-hardening.service
[Unit]
Description=Remount /tmp with noexec,nosuid,nodev
DefaultDependencies=no
After=tmp.mount local-fs-pre.target
Before=local-fs.target
Requires=tmp.mount
ConditionPathIsMountPoint=/tmp

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=/bin/mount -o remount,bind,noexec,nosuid,nodev /tmp

[Install]
WantedBy=local-fs.target
EOF
echo ---
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable tmp-hardening.service 2>&1
